earnings.title: ITT REPORTS THIRD QUARTER 2026 EPS OF $1.38
highlights: Revenue grew 44% to $1.4 billion, 8% organic, led by SPX FLOW and strong performance in connectors and pump pr ojects
Revenue increased 44% to $1.4 billion versus prior year with SPX FLOW contributing 35 points of growth.

Organic revenue increased 8%, led by strength across Connect & Control Technologies (CCT) aerospace and defense connectors, as well as continued momentum in pump projects and valves within Flow Technologies (FT).

Third quarter operating income increased 26% to $227 million, driven by operational performance from the legacy business and contributions from SPX FLOW, partially offset by acquisition-related costs.

quotes.text: ITTers around the world delivered yet another strong quarter as they executed relentlessly across the business. Our teams continue to win in the market, whilst our acquisitions are enhancing the strength of our portfolio and compounding ITT's long-term value creation.
quotes.by: ITT’s Chief Executive Officer and President Luca Savi

quotes.text: Davide is a proven leader and disciplined operator with a strong track record of delivering results.

outlook: Full-year EP S expected to be $4.65 to $4.73; adjusted EPS guidance raised to $8.54 to $8.62
Based on strong commercial and operational performance year-to-date, the company now expects organic revenue growth of 7% to 9% and total revenue growth of 41% to 43%.
Operating margin is now expected to finish the year between 13.3% and 14.1%, with adjusted operating margin of 20.2% to 21.0%, an increase of 80 to 160 bps versus prior year.
EPS is expected to be $4.65 to $4.73, with adjusted EPS of $8.54 to $8.62, representing growth of 19% to 20% for the full year.

items.heading: Our operating results have been, and may continue to be, adversely affected by unfavorable or uncertain global macroeconomic and capital market conditions.

Our business has been, and may continue to be, adversely affected by raw material price volatility, a limited number of suppliers and the inability of suppliers to meet quality and delivery requirements.

Recent mergers, acquisitions or venture investments could present operational challenges and past divestitures and spin-offs may expose us to potential liabilities, all of which could adversely affect our results of operations and financial position.

The industries in which we operate are experiencing a skilled labor shortage and if we are unable to hire and retain key personnel, including engineering talent and senior management talent, our ability to operate or grow our business could be negatively impacted.

Failure to provide high quality and reliable products, innovate or respond to competitors in our markets or protect our intellectual property rights could adversely impact our business and financial results.
Our operations could be disrupted, and our business could be materially and adversely affected by our inability to prevent, detect or adequately respond to cybersecurity breaches.
